newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's April public sector deficit $504 mln.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's April public sector deficit $504 mln.

text.p: Argentina ran up a public sector deficit of $504 million in April, up from a $496 million shortfall in April 1996, the Economy Ministry said Monday.
Economy Secretary Pablo Guidotti told reporters the April deficit the result of $5.61 billion in expenditures and $5.1 billion in revenues.
Guidotti also said the government was confident it would meet the $360 million public sector deficit target for the second quarter agreed upon with the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
"The second quarter targets are tight...but we will be able to meet them," he said.
The country did better than expected in the first quarter, accumulating a public sector deficit of $885 million compared with a target shortfall of $1.04 billion.
Guidotti said June figures were looking up for two reasons -- unlike May, there will be no debt interest payment maturities, and revenues from corporate taxes are due.
The official said corporate tax revenues were now expected to be higher than originally thought but declined to discuss specific figures.
